newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet resumes scheduled flight service to Boston.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet resumes scheduled flight service to Boston.

text.p: ValuJet Inc. said it resumed scheduled service to Boston on Thursday with five daily roundtrip flights from Atlanta and four from Washington's Dulles International Airport.
The discount carrier waived its advance purchase requirement for travel by March 31, saying it would sell every seat between Atlanta and Boston for $89 and between Washington and Boston for $49.
Boston travelers connecting to or from Florida also would be able to fly $99 one-way. Connecting flights from Boston to other Southeast markets would cost $109 one-way.
"Air travelers have seen fares return to unreasonably expensive levels in cities where ValuJet has yet to return," Valujet Airlines President Joseph Corr said.
"Boston is a prime example. With ValuJet absent from the market, leisure fares between Atlanta and Boston increased 133 percent and business fares increased more than 250 percent."
After March 31, one-way fares between Atlanta and Boston would range from $89 to $149. One-way fares between Washington Dulles and Boston would cost $49 to $99.
